subtitle: Monthly horror picks for the mortally curious.
vote_instructions: Vote for as many novels and short works as you're interested in.

novels.title: There Is No Antimemetics Division
novels.author: qntm (2025)
novels.vibe: Cosmic-dread puzzle box with a surprisingly aching human heart.
novels.summary: Inside a secret organization, a small team fights entities that erase themselves from memory, so knowledge of them vanishes almost as soon as it's learned, along with colleagues, loved ones, and even their own goals. Revised and expanded from its original SCP Foundation-era web serial, this edition is equal parts mind-bending sci-fi and existential horror.
novels.warnings: Violence and death, existential/cosmic dread, memory loss, grief, mental distress.

novels.title: Exoskeleton
novels.author: Shane Stadler (2012)
novels.vibe: A pulpy sci-fi, suspense and government-conspiracy mash-up with a trapped-in-the-experiment feel.
novels.summary: A convicted felon is offered a choice: serve a 25-year prison sentence, or spend 365 days in a new experimental corrections program. He picks the program and quickly regrets it. A genre blend of science fiction, suspense, and horror, and the first book in a longer series.
novels.warnings: Graphic violence and torture, prison setting, human experimentation, government conspiracy themes.

novels.title: Blood Music
novels.author: Greg Bear (1985)
novels.vibe: Big-idea biological horror that goes from lab accident to world-changing in a hurry.
novels.summary: A rogue biotech researcher, fired for exceeding his authorization, injects himself with intelligent cells he engineered in the lab to save his work. The cells begin to change him, and then everything around him. Expanded from Bear's award-winning 1983 novelette, it's a landmark of body horror and sci-fi.
novels.warnings: Body horror, loss of bodily autonomy, infection and mass death, apocalyptic themes.

novels.title: The Body Snatchers
novels.author: Jack Finney (1955)
novels.vibe: Paranoid small-town invasion thriller, the origin of 'they're not who they seem.'
novels.summary: In a quiet California town, Dr. Miles Bennell's patients start insisting that their loved ones have been replaced by identical impostors. As he digs in, Miles discovers that something has arrived in town, and that it's spreading. The novel behind four film adaptations (including 1956's Invasion of the Body Snatchers).
novels.warnings: Violence and death, paranoia, loss of identity, period-typical sexism.

short_works.title: All Tomorrows
short_works.author: C.M. Kösemen (2006)
short_works.vibe: A cold, awe-struck speculative-evolution chronicle of what humanity could become.
short_works.summary: An illustrated, billion-year chronicle of humanity's strange and often grim descendants, shaped by both natural evolution and genetic engineering, some of it at the hands of a mysterious and far superior alien species. Originally released as a free online PDF, it became an internet cult classic before getting its first print edition.
short_works.warnings: Body horror, themes of enslavement and genetic manipulation, extinction, dehumanization.

short_works.title: Sandkings
short_works.author: George R.R. Martin (1979)
short_works.vibe: Mean-spirited creature horror about cruelty coming back around.
short_works.summary: Simon Kress, a wealthy collector of exotic pets, buys a terrarium of tiny insect-like creatures called sandkings that form warring colonies he feeds, torments, and watches for sport. Then the colonies start to take notice of him. Winner of the Hugo and Nebula awards.
short_works.warnings: Animal cruelty (including a puppy), graphic violence and gore, torture, death.

short_works.title: The Last Question
short_works.author: Isaac Asimov (1956)
short_works.vibe: Awe and melancholy on a cosmic timescale, closer to wonder than horror.
short_works.summary: Across the whole of human history, generation after generation asks a vast supercomputer one question: can entropy be reversed? Asimov's own favorite among his stories, and a far lighter pick for the month's theme than the others.
short_works.warnings: Heat death of the universe, human extinction (non-graphic).

short_works.title: The Autopsy
short_works.author: Michael Shea (1980)
short_works.vibe: Grisly, claustrophobic dissection horror with a creeping cosmic edge.
short_works.summary: A pathologist is sent to an isolated Colorado mining town to determine what killed a group of miners in an explosion, and finds the truth is far stranger than a bomb. A Hugo and Nebula nominee, adapted for Netflix's Cabinet of Curiosities in 2022.
short_works.warnings: Graphic gore, detailed dissection and body horror, parasitic possession, terminal illness, violence, death.
